records.issue_text: [BUG] Routine, successful cleanup batches are logged at Error level via r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ...), including the full slice of IDs, in the MaxAge path of CleanAnnotations. Every annotation cleanup cycle emits error-level log lines with potentially thousands of IDs per batch, permanently polluting operator alerting on error-level logs and ballooning log volume; the trailing "err", err field is always nil because the error branch already returned before the log call.
records.rationale: In `CleanAnnotations` (MaxAge path), after successfully fetching IDs it unconditionally logs at error level: `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err)` and similarly after deletion. These log lines include the full `ids` slice and the `"err", err` field will be nil because the `if err != nil { return 0, err }` branch returns before the log call. This will emit error-level logs on routine successful cleanup batches, potentially with thousands of IDs, which is an observable behavior defect introduced by the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteByIDs only special-cases the SQLite 999-parameter limit; the placeholder path is used unconditionally on Postgres and MySQL regardless of batch size, and Postgres's wire-protocol bind limit (32767 parameters) is not guarded. A user who sets annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size above 32767 on Postgres gets every batch failing with a bind-parameter error ("bind message has N result formats..."), so annotation cleanup stops deleting anything and the cleanup job errors each cycle — the exact failure mode the SQLite workaround was added to prevent, reintroduced for another backend.
records.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, the only safeguard against too many bound parameters is a SQLite-only branch: `if r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit { ... } else { placeholders := "?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1) ... }`. For Postgres/MySQL the `else` path always creates one placeholder per ID and binds `len(ids)` parameters, with no upper bound besides the configured `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` (used to fetch IDs). The diff adds a test explicitly setting batch size to 32767 for SQLite, showing large batch sizes are intended/possible; w

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] untilDoneOrCancelled treats a batch that fetched IDs but deleted 0 rows (e.g. rows removed by a concurrent cleanup process or overlapping instance between fetchIDs and deleteByIDs, which run in separate sessions) as 'done' and exits the loop early, conflating 'nothing to fetch' with 'nothing deleted'. A single lost race truncates that cleanup pass, leaving annotations/tags that meet the deletion criteria in place until the next cycle; with the MaxCount rule this means retention limits are transiently violated. Self-healing on the next run, but the termination signal is wrong.
records.rationale: In the new batching logic, `untilDoneOrCancelled` terminates when the callback reports `affected == 0` (end-of-work signal). Under concurrency, it’s possible to fetch a non-empty `ids` slice but have `deleteByIDs` delete 0 rows (e.g., another instance deleted them between the two sessions). records.issue_text: [BUG] Cleanup progress is logged at Error level with an always-nil `err` field, so every successful cleanup batch emits an error-severity log line. Operators running annotation cleanup see recurring `logger=annotations.cleanup level=error msg="Annotations to clean by time" err=null` lines (five such sites in CleanAnnotations/CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags, each also dumping the full ids slice, up to batch-size entries, and the SQL condition). On a large cleanup this floods error logs and alerting on level=error, and the logged `err` field can never contain a real error at these sites because `fetchIDs` errors are returned before the log statement executes — the line misdirects debugging toward a nil error during incident triage.
